text:
Did You Know This App You Use Every Day Was Created By A Former IAF Pilot?
Curated By :
Last Updated:
Today, the app serves over 4 million homes across more than 25,000 communities in over 50 cities.
1/10
Urban life especially in high-rise societies comes with its own set of challenges. One app has slowly become part of many residents’ daily routines that has made their life easy. It allows users to pre-approve guests, track delivery personnel and receive instant notifications when visitors arrive. For countless apartment communities, it acts like a digital guardian for security and communication. But the story behind the app is less known. It began with someone whose life was shaped by the skies and the discipline of the armed forces.
2/10
And that name is Arisetty Vijay Kumar who grew up with an interest in aviation and service to the country. According to reports, he trained at the National Defence Academy to prepare for a career in the Indian Air Force (IAF). He was commissioned In IAF in 1999 and specialised as a flying pilot (F(P)) with Service Number 25858.
ADVERTISEMENT
3/10
During his time in the Air Force, he flew helicopters for rescue operations and peacekeeping assignments where he had to sometimes fly in difficult terrain or under extreme weather conditions. With each mission, his skills developed because quick decision-making could mean all the difference between life and death. The discipline of military life and flying under pressure helped him learn how to solve difficult problems.
4/10
A turning point came in December 2004 during the Indian Ocean tsunami. Stationed in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Arisetty faced a crisis as massive waves struck the region. Without hesitation, he helped evacuate personnel. He guided them to higher ground on the airfield runway. He also participated in helicopter missions where he had to rescue people from rooftops and other risky locations. His bravery and determination during this disaster earned him the Shaurya Chakra, one of India's highest peacetime gallantry honours, in 2005.
ADVERTISEMENT
5/10
Despite a promising military career, Arisetty’s path shifted unexpectedly due to a severe shoulder injury he suffered during a sports activity. The injury made him medically unfit to continue flying and he retired from IAF after 14 years. Leaving the structured environment of military life required a major adjustment. But this change opened the door for him to explore new opportunities and think about how his skills could be applied outside the armed forces.
6/10
After retirement, Arisetty focused on building knowledge in the business world. He studied at the Indian School of Business in Hyderabad and later worked at Goldman Sachs where he gained experience in corporate management and operations. While working there, he noticed problems in city life especially in gated communities. There were issues like visitor management, delivery tracking and security. These problems gave him the idea to create a platform that could make life easier and safer for residents.
ADVERTISEMENT
7/10
In 2016, Arisetty teamed up with Abhishek Kumar and Shreyans Daga to create MyGate. The platform was designed to handle visitor verification, package tracking, emergency alerts and communication between residents, security personnel and society management. It transformed the way gated communities operated. The app combined technology and practical solutions to address real problems in urban societies.
8/10
MyGate expanded as more communities adopted the platform. It addressed gaps like outdated security processes and slow communication. Residents could now approve visitors remotely, track deliveries in real-time and receive instant notifications. The platform also allowed society management to handle property transactions, helpdesk requests and emergency alerts in one place.
ADVERTISEMENT
9/10
Under Arisetty’s leadership, the platform grew steadily and gained millions of users. Communities appreciated the structured approach to security and the ability to manage day-to-day operations through a single app. As the number of users increased, so did the platform’s capabilities as it handled large volumes of requests and ensured smooth operation for residents and staff at the same time.
